tytul: Roasted cherry tomatoes in olive oil for the refrigerator, eaten by the next day
wstep: This card is for cherry tomatoes roasted in olive oil, kept in the refrigerator and eaten soon. This card follows a general rule for vegetables in oil from food-safety authorities, not a recipe tested for this product. It gives no amounts or cooking times; it gives the rules for preparing and storing it. The German Federal Institute for Risk Assessment (BfR) says homemade vegetables in oil are kept in the refrigerator and eaten no later than the day after they are made. The Swedish Food Agency (Livsmedelsverket) also says homemade vegetables in oil that have not been heat-treated are kept in the refrigerator.

ostrzezenia.tekst: Keep the refrigerator at 40 °F (4 °C) or lower.
Eat them no later than the day after you make them, and throw away what is left.

Never keep them at room temperature: vegetables in oil, including partly dried ones, give C. botulinum good conditions to grow (no oxygen, the pH and the water in the vegetables), and at room temperature the bacterium can multiply quickly.

Do not make them in advance to store: the BfR says that with vegetables in oil a household cannot make sure that C. botulinum will not grow and form toxin, and it advises against making such products in advance for storage.

akapity: Appearance, smell and taste cannot tell you whether vegetables in oil carry a botulism hazard.
There are no validated processes for vegetables and herbs in oil made at home; in the USA, the rules for such products apply only to commercial processors.
According to the Swedish Food Agency, cooking vegetables in oil could in theory inactivate C. botulinum spores, but there are no studies confirming that the method works in practice.
So this card treats roasted cherry tomatoes in oil like any other vegetables in oil.
Make only as much as you will eat by the day after you make it.
Start with a clean glass container: wash it thoroughly and boil it for 10 minutes.
Choose good-quality cherry tomatoes, wash them thoroughly and pat them dry.
Keep the tomatoes in oil in the refrigerator at 40 °F (4 °C) or lower.
Eat them no later than the day after you made them, and throw away what is left.
